report.summary: Two cross-file patterns found: (1) shared guard functions re-exported by DeepSeek but defined in daedalus/lanes/checks, and (2) implicit contract that _strip_comments_generic handles block comments, contradicted by its code.
risks: DeepSeek provider re-exports guard functions from daedalus/lanes/checks, but the shared module is not shown in any report; if those functions have side effects or dependencies not visible in the provider, they could behave unexpectedly.

_strip_comments_generic in clones.py claims block comment awareness but the visible code only handles line comments; block comment handling may be incomplete or missing, leading to false clone positives.
todos: Verify daedalus/lanes/checks module to confirm guard functions have no hidden side effects.
Review full _strip_comments_generic implementation to ensure block comments are handled correctly.

hypotheses.claim: DeepSeek provider re-exports guard functions from daedalus/lanes/checks, but those functions are defined in a shared module not shown in any report; their behavior may have side effects or dependencies that the provider does not control.
hypotheses.mechanism: deepseek.py imports and re-exports _toplevel_defs, _substitution_reason, _unresolved_first_party_imports from daedalus.lanes.checks. The provider assumes these are pure and safe, but the shared module's implementation is not visible in any scan report. If those functions have I/O, network, or other side effects, the provider's claim of no side effects is violated.
hypotheses.refuted_by: If daedalus/lanes/checks is inspected and found to contain only pure functions with no side effects, this hypothesis is refuted.

hypotheses.claim: _strip_comments_generic in clones.py claims to handle block comments via spec.block_comment, but the visible code only processes line comment markers; block comments are not handled, contradicting the documented behavior.
hypotheses.mechanism: The function iterates through source text, checking for line comment markers from spec.line_comment. The docstring mentions spec.block_comment but the code shown does not use it. If block comments are not stripped, they remain in normalized source, causing false positive clone matches (identical code with different block comments would hash the same, while different block comments would not be stripped).
hypotheses.refuted_by: If the full implementation of _strip_comments_generic (beyond this chunk) includes block comment handling, this hypothesis is refuted.
evidence: daedalus/structcore/clones.py: _strip_comments_generic code only uses line comment markers
